description:
Six agents from Space Engineering at Politecnico di Milano. One mission. Infinite possibilities.
Spicing up the universe, one orbit at a time.
summary: Totally SPHEREx is a public web tool that lets anyone explore the infrared sky seen by NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Enter a name or coordinates, and the tool shows the SPHEREx images of that spot as a time-lapse, so you can spot objects that move or change. For each target it extracts a spectrum from 0.75 to 5 µm and looks for molecular signatures such as water, methane and CO₂, with their uncertainties. Known objects from SIMBAD are overlaid on the map with plain-language cards, and users can flag anything they cannot identify for the community to review. The tool never downloads the full archive: it requests only small cutouts around the target, so it runs on a laptop. Four difficulty levels, two languages and shareable links make it usable by students and researchers alike.
details: Totally SPHEREx is a web tool that turns NASA's SPHEREx archive into something anyone can watch and question. Type a name or coordinates and it shows that patch of sky as a time-lapse across SPHEREx visits and wavelengths, builds a 0.75–5 µm spectrum of the target, and checks it for molecular features such as water, methane and CO₂, with uncertainties. It never downloads the full archive: a Python backend (Flask, Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, SQLite) requests only small cutouts from NASA/IRSA, cleans and aligns them, and caches them locally, while the front end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript with Aladin Lite) overlays known objects from SIMBAD. What makes it creative is the combination: a video of one object through time and colour instead of a static map, four levels from guided explorer to researcher in two languages, and community pins that let anyone flag an unidentified object for others to confirm.
